title: review: G8: semantic review triggers (authorization, migrations, public interfaces, dependencies) next to security_paths, and review approval bound to the reviewed commit and re-assessed after a rebase that changes the diff
spec:
Depends on G7 (T-0272, daemon.py) and G2b (T-0267, merge.py). Today daemon.gate() decides the review policy from changed_paths against [review].security_paths globs only; a review's verdict is stored as review_verdict on the review task and on the source task without the commit it looked at; merge_reviewed() then calls merge.merge, which rebases the task branch onto goal/<parent> and runs tests, so a rebase with real conflicts resolved or with semantic drift still merges under the old approval. The analysis: security-path review alone misses consequential changes; add semantic triggers; bind approval to the reviewed changes and reassess after meaningful rebase changes.
Change:
1. pool.toml [review] gains semantic_paths (globs, defaults: pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Dockerfile*, docker/**, **/migrations/**, orchestrator/serve.py, orchestrator/mcp.py, orchestrator/bus_mcp.py, orchestrator/cli.py) and semantic_patterns (regexes matched against added lines of the diff, defaults: authorization words such as bearer, token, authenticate, authorize, permission; ALTER TABLE or create table; __all__ =; @mcp.tool or add_parser(; def with a public name whose signature changed is out of scope). daemon.gate() evaluates security_paths first (unchanged), then semantic_paths, then semantic_patterns over `git diff <base>..<head>` added lines; review_reason records semantic_path:<glob> or semantic_pattern:<name>; one review on security_review_tier with the checklist, same as security paths.
2. Binding: when the daemon creates a review task it stores reviewed_sha = the task branch head on the review task and pipeline.reviewed_sha on the source task; merge_reviewed() checks the branch head before merging: if it moved past reviewed_sha, the approval is void: reset reviews_expected accounting, spawn a fresh review (notify), do not merge. In merge.merge, after the rebase, compute the diff hash of goal..branch before and after the rebase (git diff with --stat and content hashed); if the rebased diff differs from the reviewed diff (conflicts resolved or rebase altered hunks) and the task had a review, stop before the fast-forward and return status 'rebase_changed_diff' so merge_reviewed holds the task with hold_reason 'merge rebase_changed_diff' for a re-review; a clean rebase that only moves the base keeps the approval.
3. README Pipeline: semantic triggers and the binding rule; pool.toml comments.
Tests in tests/test_daemon.py: test_semantic_path_triggers_review, test_semantic_pattern_triggers_review, test_review_records_reviewed_sha, test_head_moved_after_approval_spawns_new_review; tests/test_merge.py::test_rebase_changing_diff_returns_status, ::test_clean_rebase_keeps_approval.
acceptance: pool.toml [review] documents semantic_paths and semantic_patterns; README updated
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: _diff_hash returns None on any git error (nonzero returncode from `git diff --stat`/`--binary`), and merge() only runs the rebase-changed-diff guard when both before_diff and after_diff are non-None. A transient git failure on either call silently skips the reviewed_sha approval-binding check and lets the merge proceed, unlike the rebase-conflict path just below which fails closed with status="failed". No test covers this failure mode.

_added_diff_lines returns None on any nonzero returncode from its own git diff call, and _matching_semantic_pattern treats that as "no match" rather than failing closed. This contradicts changed_paths()'s documented fail-closed contract (diff_unavailable) that the rest of _review_plan relies on: if the first diff call (name-only) succeeds but this second, independent diff call (--unified=0) fails, semantic pattern detection is silently skipped and the task can merge with review_reason "none" despite containing a matched-worthy authorization/schema/export/tool change.
